beat_label: The Dark Days begin: districts rebel against the Capitol
session_desc: The districts rise up against the Capitol, triggering a nationwide civil war. The conflict spreads rapidly and reshapes Panem through violence, scarcity, and surveillance.

motivations.Capitol: Crush the uprising and preserve total control over Panem.
motivations.Rebel Districts: Win freedom from exploitation and political domination.
motivations.District 13: Provide military capacity and coordination to sustain the rebellion.

beat_label: The Capitol escalates: engineered weapons and mass surveillance
session_desc: To regain control, the Capitol deploys advanced military technology and genetically engineered tools, including insect and bird surveillance programs, to identify and terrorize rebels.

motivations.Capitol: Break rebel coordination by tracking, intimidating, and punishing resistance networks.
motivations.Rebel Districts: Adapt to surveillance and keep organizing despite overwhelming force.

beat_label: Siege of the Capitol; wartime propaganda and public executions
session_desc: As rebel forces tighten a siege on the Capitol, shortages worsen. The Capitol responds with propaganda and high-profile executions, turning civic spaces into political theater.

motivations.Capitol: Maintain morale and deter dissent by staging fear and loyalty as spectacle.
motivations.Rebel Districts: Force a surrender by cutting supply lines and pressuring the Capitol’s leadership.

beat_label: District 13 ceasefire; the rebellion collapses; districts are pacified
session_desc: District 13 strikes a ceasefire to secure its own survival and disappears underground. The Capitol presents 13 as destroyed, and with its support gone, the rebellion collapses; the remaining districts are forced back under Capitol rule.

motivations.District 13: Guarantee survival through deterrence and secrecy rather than total victory.
motivations.Capitol: End the war without triggering mutually assured destruction, then reassert authority.
motivations.Rebel Districts: Survive defeat while facing renewed repression and punitive measures.

beat_label: Treaty of Treason; the Hunger Games are instituted
session_desc: The Capitol codifies the Treaty of Treason, introducing new laws to prevent rebellion and establishing the Hunger Games as an annual punishment and reminder of defeat.

motivations.Capitol: Make obedience permanent through ritualized punishment, fear, and spectacle.
motivations.Districts: Endure the imposed system and protect families under strict control.

beat_label: The early Hunger Games begin in the Capitol Arena (years 1–9)
session_title: Early Games in a fixed arena
session_desc: The first decade of Hunger Games is hosted in a Capitol arena, establishing the yearly ritual and the broadcast-driven punishment system that the trilogy’s characters inherit.

motivations.Capitol: Normalize the Games as entertainment and deterrence; build a tradition that enforces hierarchy.
motivations.Districts: Survive grief and coercion while minimizing additional punishment.
motivations.Tributes: Stay alive under impossible conditions, often without meaningful support.

beat_label: First Victory Tour; Games move beyond the Capitol stadium
session_desc: The Capitol introduces the Victory Tour and experiments with arenas outside the main stadium, extending the Games’ influence into districts as a traveling display of power.

motivations.Capitol: Shape public memory in each district and keep fear active year-round.
motivations.Victors: Survive politically by performing gratitude and compliance under scrutiny.
motivations.Districts: Endure renewed trauma as the Capitol forces participation in the victor narrative.

beat_label: Annual Games continue (years 12–19): a tradition hardens
session_desc: With the yearly pattern established, the Capitol reinforces the Games as a fixed part of life: reaping, preparation, broadcasts, and district mourning become predictable—by design.

motivations.Capitol: Make oppression feel inevitable and self-perpetuating through repetition.
motivations.Districts: Develop coping strategies and quiet resistance while prioritizing survival.

session_desc: By the early 20s, the Games are no longer just punishment—they’re a central Capitol broadcast, enabling public narrative control and reinforcing district isolation.

motivations.Capitol: Expand spectacle to command attention and rewrite fear as entertainment.
motivations.Districts: Avoid retaliation and protect families under increasingly public scrutiny.
motivations.Tributes: Survive while navigating Capitol expectations that can be as dangerous as the arena.

beat_label: First Quarter Quell: districts must choose their tributes
session_desc: For the first Quarter Quell, the Capitol changes the rules: instead of a random reaping, districts are forced to elect their own tributes—weaponizing internal blame and division as punishment.

motivations.Capitol: Prove it can rewrite rules at will and turn districts against themselves.
motivations.District Citizens: Protect loved ones while being forced into coerced, divisive choices.
motivations.District Leaders: Comply while limiting backlash and keeping order under surveillance.
motivations.Tributes: Survive after being selected through a system designed to fracture community support.

session_desc: Capitol City — The Second Quarter Quell is announced: districts must send twice as many tributes, raising the stakes and reinforcing the Capitol’s control.

motivations.Snow: Use the Quarter Quell twist to reassert fear and remind Panem the Capitol sets the rules.
motivations.Capitol: Turn the announcement into spectacle and obedience messaging.

session_desc: Arena / District 12 — A District 12 tribute exploits a force-field boundary to turn the Capitol’s weapons against itself; afterward the Capitol retaliates against his loved ones to punish defiance.

motivations.Haymitch: Survive by reading the arena’s hidden mechanics and using them at the decisive moment.
motivations.Capitol: Make an example of clever resistance so other victors stay compliant.

beat_label: District 12: public hanging and the ‘Hanging Tree’
session_title: A public execution becomes a song
session_desc: District 12 — A young Katniss witnesses a public hanging; the condemned person’s final words become the basis of the ‘Hanging Tree’ song that later resurfaces as rebellion symbolism.

motivations.Katniss: Process fear and grief, and remember the moment that taught her what the Capitol does to dissent.
motivations.District 12: Keep its head down while absorbing the warning intended for everyone.

beat_label: District 12: tesserae and the reaping system
session_desc: District 12 — Gale takes tesserae to feed his family, multiplying his entries in future reapings and showing how hunger is weaponized to maintain control.

motivations.Gale: Keep his siblings alive even though it increases his odds of being reaped.
motivations.District 12: Trade risk for food because there are no safe choices under scarcity.

session_desc: District 12 Seam — A mining explosion kills many workers, including Katniss’s father (and Gale’s), collapsing families’ livelihoods overnight.

motivations.Katniss: Hold the family together as grief and hunger threaten to break them.
motivations.Gale: Step into adult responsibility fast to protect his siblings.
motivations.Mother: Survive grief and return to caring for her children.
motivations.District 12: Endure loss because the Capitol’s economy treats miners as expendable.

session_desc: District 12 woods / Hob — Katniss begins hunting and trading to keep her family alive, entering the woods illegally and building the routines that define her later survival.

motivations.Katniss: Secure food and prevent Prim from starving.
motivations.Prim: Trust Katniss and cling to the hope she brings home.
motivations.Mother: Recover enough to help while relying on Katniss’s strength.

session_desc: District 12 — After Katniss is turned away hungry, Peeta deliberately burns bread and throws it to her, giving her a turning-point memory of kindness under cruelty.

motivations.Katniss: Find a way for her family to eat another day.
motivations.Peeta: Help Katniss without drawing attention, even if it risks punishment.

session_desc: District 12 woods — Katniss and Gale meet while hunting beyond the fence, forming a partnership built on shared risk, survival skills, and resentment toward the Capitol.

motivations.Katniss: Improve her hunting and keep her family alive through reliable trade.
motivations.Gale: Find allies who understand the cost of survival and share his anger.

session_title: Katniss buys a goat for Prim
session_desc: District 12 — Katniss trades hard-won goods to buy a goat so Prim can have milk, a rare investment in long-term survival.

motivations.Katniss: Give Prim something stable and nourishing beyond daily scavenging.
motivations.Prim: Care for the goat and contribute to the household’s survival.
motivations.District 12: Barter constantly because money and security mean little here.

session_title: A tense truce at the Hob
session_desc: The Hob — Katniss navigates trade, distrust, and quiet solidarity among neighbors who all live under surveillance and scarcity.

motivations.Katniss: Make trades without attracting Peacekeeper attention.
motivations.District 12: Help each other just enough to get by without becoming targets.

session_desc: Capitol City — The Hunger Games machine continues to professionalize: stylists, interviews, and arena engineering become even more central to the Capitol’s propaganda.

motivations.Capitol: Keep districts afraid and entertained by making the Games irresistible spectacle.

session_desc: District 12 woods — Katniss and Gale talk seriously about running away into the wild, a fragile plan that collides with the inevitability of the reaping.

motivations.Katniss: Protect her family while imagining a life without Capitol rules.
motivations.Gale: Push for rebellion-by-leaving and refuse to accept the system as permanent.

session_desc: District 12 woods — Katniss and Gale hunt and talk through the dread of reaping day, weighing survival against the system’s cruelty.

motivations.Katniss: Keep her family fed and steady herself before Prim’s first reaping.
motivations.Gale: Support Katniss and vent his anger at the tessera system.

session_desc: District 12 square — Prim’s name is drawn; Katniss volunteers in her place and Peeta is selected as the male tribute, setting the Games in motion.

motivations.Katniss: Protect Prim at any cost.
motivations.Prim: Survive the shock and cling to Katniss.
motivations.Peeta: Face the selection and keep composure.
motivations.Gale: Reach Katniss and Prim despite being powerless.

session_desc: Train to the Capitol — Katniss and Peeta learn what it means to be ‘sellable’ while Haymitch tests them, pushing for discipline that might keep them alive.

motivations.Katniss: Figure out how to survive the Capitol’s rules without losing herself.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss while staying observant about the political game.
motivations.Haymitch: Forge a survivable image and strategy for his tributes.
motivations.Effie: Deliver polished tributes to the Capitol machine.

session_desc: Capitol prep — Cinna and the team craft an unforgettable look, turning Katniss into a symbol to attract sponsors and attention.

motivations.Katniss: Endure the transformation and learn how performance affects survival.
motivations.Cinna: Create a striking, meaningful image that gives Katniss leverage.
motivations.Peeta: Play along while reading how the Capitol reacts.
motivations.Portia: Help present Peeta in a complementary way.

session_desc: Training Center — Katniss watches the Careers and other tributes, learning who is dangerous and which skills matter in the arena.

motivations.Katniss: Assess threats and choose skills that fit her strengths.
motivations.Careers: Show dominance and scout weaker tributes.
motivations.Gamemakers: Stage the process as controlled spectacle.

session_title: Peeta’s social play and sponsor angle
session_desc: Training Center — Peeta begins building goodwill with other tributes, hinting at how social perception and sponsors can be as crucial as weapons.

motivations.Peeta: Increase sponsor potential by appearing likable and cooperative.
motivations.Katniss: Stay wary while learning to use perception strategically.

session_desc: Training Center — Katniss focuses on practical survival skills and stealth, preparing to outlast stronger tributes rather than outfight them.

motivations.Katniss: Build a survival plan centered on speed, stealth, and endurance.

session_title: Rue’s attention: a quiet potential ally
session_desc: Training Center — Rue observes Katniss and subtly signals interest in teaming up, suggesting alliance beyond the Career pack.

motivations.Katniss: Notice who might be trustworthy in a hostile setting.
motivations.Rue: Seek a partner who can protect her and share information.

beat_label: Capitol: training scores and first shocks
session_desc: Training Center — Tributes face private evaluation, learning that the Capitol judges them as entertainment as much as fighters.

motivations.Katniss: Prove competence without revealing everything.
motivations.Gamemakers: Rank tributes to shape the story audiences will follow.

beat_label: Capitol: training scores and first shocks
session_title: Arrow at the Gamemakers; high score
session_desc: Training Center — Ignored by officials, Katniss fires an arrow into their meal to demand attention, earning a rare high score and attracting both sponsors and enemies.

motivations.Katniss: Force the Capitol to take her seriously.
motivations.Gamemakers: Contain disruption while turning it into narrative.
motivations.Cato: Target the tribute who challenged the system publicly.

session_desc: Capitol — Cinna coaches Katniss on how to project confidence and authenticity, treating image as a survival tool rather than vanity.

motivations.Katniss: Learn to perform without feeling owned.
motivations.Cinna: Give Katniss agency through a controlled public persona.

session_desc: Capitol — Haymitch pushes the ‘star-crossed’ angle and drills Katniss and Peeta on what to reveal, building a sponsor plan before the arena.

motivations.Haymitch: Secure sponsor attention that translates into supplies.
motivations.Katniss: Endure the script while keeping her priorities straight.
motivations.Peeta: Support the plan while protecting Katniss emotionally.

session_title: Katniss and Peeta on Caesar’s stage
session_desc: Capitol — Under bright lights, Katniss performs confidence while Peeta plays sincerity, turning their relationship into a story the Capitol can consume.

motivations.Katniss: Stay compelling and in control to attract sponsors.
motivations.Peeta: Protect Katniss by shaping the narrative around her.
motivations.Caesar: Deliver a show that makes violence palatable.

session_desc: Capitol — Peeta reveals he has long loved Katniss, reframing them as tragic lovers and provoking Katniss’s anger at being used as a plot device.

motivations.Peeta: Increase their sponsor value and keep Katniss alive.
motivations.Katniss: Resist being manipulated while staying alive.
motivations.Haymitch: Exploit the angle to secure resources.

session_desc: Arena — Tributes rise into the arena; a violent scramble at the Cornucopia begins, forcing immediate choices between supplies and survival.

motivations.Katniss: Grab essentials and escape alive.
motivations.Peeta: Protect Katniss if possible while avoiding immediate death.
motivations.Careers: Secure weapons and eliminate threats quickly.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss hides, counts alliances, and learns how quickly the Capitol’s rules turn people into prey.

motivations.Katniss: Stay unseen long enough to form a plan.

session_desc: Arena — Dehydration becomes the primary threat as Katniss searches for a water source while staying ahead of the Career pack.

motivations.Katniss: Find water without being cornered.

session_desc: Arena — Rue helps Katniss evade danger and they form a cautious alliance based on information-sharing and complementary skills.

motivations.Katniss: Accept help without surrendering control.
motivations.Rue: Survive by partnering with someone stronger.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss studies the Careers’ stockpile and routines, looking for a way to weaken them without direct combat.

motivations.Katniss: Find leverage that doesn’t require head-on fighting.
motivations.Careers: Protect their supplies and dominate the field.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss drops a tracker jacker nest onto the Careers, creating chaos, gaining supplies, and earning an enemy in Cato.

motivations.Katniss: Break the Career advantage and escape.

session_desc: Arena — Rue shares what she’s learned about edible plants and enemy movement, shifting their alliance from survival to sabotage.

motivations.Katniss: Use information to level the playing field.
motivations.Rue: Contribute expertise and keep their plan quiet.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss uses a fire-starting signal plan to destroy the Careers’ supplies, forcing them into desperation and changing the balance of power.

motivations.Katniss: Remove the Careers’ material advantage.
motivations.Rue: Execute the signal safely from cover.

session_desc: Arena — Rue is caught and mortally wounded, turning Katniss’s alliance into grief and rage against the Capitol’s spectacle.

motivations.Rue: Survive long enough to warn Katniss.
motivations.Katniss: Reach Rue and stop the attacker.
motivations.Marvel: Secure a kill to impress sponsors and Careers.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss decorates Rue’s body with flowers and salutes District 11, an act of mourning that becomes open defiance broadcast to all districts.

motivations.Katniss: Honor Rue and reject the Capitol’s dehumanization.
motivations.District 11: Receive the message and feel solidarity.
motivations.Capitol: Contain the emotional impact while keeping the show running.

session_desc: Arena — The Capitol announces a feast at the Cornucopia to lure tributes into conflict, using need as a weapon.

motivations.Capitol: Force confrontations to raise drama.
motivations.Katniss: Decide whether to risk everything for medicine.

session_desc: Arena — Hearing Peeta is injured, Katniss chooses to risk the feast for medicine, shifting her priority from solitary survival to protecting him.

motivations.Katniss: Keep Peeta alive despite the trap.
motivations.Peeta: Survive long enough for help and avoid slowing Katniss.

session_desc: Arena — Tributes converge on the Cornucopia; the feast becomes a coordinated trap that turns scarcity into violence.

motivations.Katniss: Get medicine and escape.
motivations.Thresh: Protect his own chances and punish threats.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss is overpowered by Clove but spared by Thresh in Rue’s name; she escapes with the medicine for Peeta.

motivations.Katniss: Survive the encounter and keep the medicine.
motivations.Thresh: Honor Rue’s alliance by sparing Katniss.

session_desc: Arena — In a hidden shelter, Katniss treats Peeta’s injuries using sponsor medicine, turning survival into caretaking under constant threat.

motivations.Katniss: Keep Peeta alive and stable.
motivations.Peeta: Recover without endangering Katniss.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss and Peeta lean into the lovers narrative to secure sponsor gifts, blurring performance and genuine dependence.

motivations.Katniss: Get supplies by playing the Capitol’s story.
motivations.Peeta: Reassure Katniss and sustain their public narrative.
motivations.Capitol: Reward drama that keeps viewers invested.

session_desc: Arena — Environmental hazards and announcements push remaining tributes toward confrontation, preventing quiet hiding from lasting.

motivations.Katniss: Stay ahead of engineered danger.
motivations.Peeta: Move despite weakness and protect Katniss.
motivations.Capitol: Force tributes into decisive conflict.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss and Peeta plan their next moves around finding food, avoiding Careers, and staying alive long enough to matter.

motivations.Katniss: Turn survival into strategy.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss while conserving strength.

session_desc: Arena — Foxface dies after eating poisonous berries, showing how knowledge gaps can be fatal even without direct combat.

motivations.Foxface: Stay alive by stealing, but a mistake proves deadly.
motivations.Capitol: Keep the arena lethal even when fights slow down.

session_desc: Arena — With fewer players left, movement becomes riskier; Katniss and Peeta must assume they’re being herded toward a finale.

motivations.Katniss: Avoid being cornered while preparing for the end.
motivations.Peeta: Stay close to Katniss and keep moving.
motivations.Cato: Hunt for the last kills to win.
motivations.Thresh: Survive alone and avoid the Careers.

session_desc: Arena — Thresh is killed off-screen, removing the last non-Career powerhouse and tightening the path to a final confrontation.

motivations.Thresh: Fight to survive alone until the end.
motivations.Capitol: Accelerate toward a dramatic finale.

session_title: Katniss and Peeta prepare for last stand
session_desc: Arena — Katniss and Peeta stock what they can and talk through what the Capitol expects from them as the last pair remaining.

motivations.Katniss: Stay ready for Cato and keep Peeta alive.
motivations.Peeta: Protect Katniss even if it costs him.

session_desc: Arena — A wall of fire drives Katniss and Peeta toward the Cornucopia, proving the Capitol controls space and fate inside the arena.

motivations.Katniss: Escape the fire without losing supplies.
motivations.Peeta: Keep pace and survive burns.
motivations.Capitol: Herd tributes to the finale location.

session_desc: Arena — Cato tracks them toward the Cornucopia, determined to finish the Games with a decisive kill.

motivations.Cato: Win by eliminating the remaining rivals.
motivations.Katniss: Avoid direct combat until she has an opening.
motivations.Peeta: Stay between Katniss and danger when possible.

session_desc: Arena — At the Cornucopia, Cato attacks; the fight turns into a desperate struggle where positioning matters more than strength.

motivations.Cato: Kill both tributes to end the Games.
motivations.Katniss: Use terrain and timing to survive and strike back.
motivations.Peeta: Hold Cato off long enough for Katniss to act.

session_desc: Arena — Mutations are released, turning the finale into a horror show and pushing all three tributes onto the Cornucopia’s structure.

motivations.Capitol: Raise terror and spectacle for the climax.
motivations.Katniss: Escape and keep Peeta alive.
motivations.Peeta: Hold on despite injury.

session_desc: Arena — Cato is trapped on the Cornucopia while mutts circle below; Katniss and Peeta endure a drawn-out standoff through the night.

motivations.Cato: Refuse to die and keep fighting for victory.
motivations.Katniss: Wait for a safe moment while staying alive.
motivations.Peeta: Hold on and keep Katniss steady.

session_desc: Arena — As the standoff drags on, Katniss weighs ending Cato’s suffering versus the risk of giving the Capitol a cleaner ending.

motivations.Katniss: End the danger and the spectacle on her own terms.
motivations.Cato: Survive, even as his situation becomes hopeless.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss shoots Cato to end the standoff, leaving her and Peeta as the last remaining tributes.

motivations.Katniss: Finish the threat and secure survival.
motivations.Cato: Fight to the end for victory.
motivations.Peeta: Survive and stay with Katniss.

session_desc: Arena — With only two tributes left, the Capitol pivots to maximize drama, setting up a rule reversal to force betrayal.

motivations.Capitol: Extract maximum spectacle from the final moment.
motivations.Seneca: Deliver an ending that satisfies Capitol appetite for control.
motivations.Katniss: Hope the rules will let them both live.
motivations.Peeta: Keep Katniss alive even if it costs him.

session_desc: Arena — The Capitol revokes the earlier promise of two victors from the same district, forcing Katniss and Peeta into an impossible choice.

motivations.Capitol: Reassert control by demanding a single winner.
motivations.Katniss: Refuse to kill Peeta and look for leverage.
motivations.Peeta: Offer himself up to spare Katniss.

session_desc: Arena — Katniss proposes a mutual suicide with nightlock berries, transforming the Capitol’s demand into a public hostage situation.

motivations.Katniss: Force the Capitol to choose between losing the Games’ ending or granting two victors.
motivations.Peeta: Follow Katniss’s lead to keep them both alive.
motivations.Capitol: Avoid a broadcast disaster that undermines the Games.

session_title: Standing at the edge of suicide
session_desc: Arena — Katniss and Peeta stand with berries ready, making the Capitol’s control visibly fragile in front of a live audience.

motivations.Katniss: Hold steady until the Capitol yields.
motivations.Peeta: Commit to the act so the threat is credible.
motivations.Capitol: Stop them without looking weak.

session_desc: Arena — The Capitol declares both Katniss and Peeta victors to preserve the spectacle, but the decision exposes the possibility of resistance.

motivations.Katniss: Survive without betraying Peeta.
motivations.Peeta: Survive with Katniss and protect her.
motivations.Capitol: Contain the damage by reframing it as romance.
motivations.Districts: Interpret the moment as a crack in Capitol power.

session_desc: Capitol — In the immediate aftermath, officials push the lovers narrative to reinterpret defiance as romance and minimize political meaning.

motivations.Katniss: Survive the debrief without incriminating herself or Peeta.
motivations.Peeta: Support the story that keeps them alive.
motivations.Caesar: Sell the ending as satisfying entertainment.
motivations.Capitol: Reclaim the narrative to prevent unrest.

session_desc: Districts — News of the double-victor defiance spreads, triggering anger and hope that begins to translate into open unrest.

motivations.Districts: Act on long-suppressed rage and the hint that resistance can work.
motivations.Capitol: Crack down before the story becomes revolution.

session_desc: Victors' Village, District 12 — Snow warns Katniss that unrest is spreading and demands she and Peeta present their finale as love to protect their families.

motivations.Katniss: Avoid retaliation against her family by convincing Snow she never meant to spark rebellion.
motivations.Snow: Reassert control by forcing Katniss into a public narrative that defuses dissent.

session_desc: District 11 Justice Building — Peeta pledges winnings to Rue and Thresh's families; Katniss publicly honors Rue and Thresh, prompting the district’s three-finger salute.

motivations.Katniss: Show respect and gratitude while trying not to inflame tensions.
motivations.Peeta: Offer tangible solidarity to Rue and Thresh’s families.
motivations.District 11 crowd: Acknowledge the gesture and express shared grief and defiance.

session_desc: Victory Tour circuit — The tour settles into a punishing routine: scripted speeches, staged dinners, and tightly controlled appearances in Districts 10 and 9.

motivations.Katniss: Get through each appearance without mistakes that could trigger punishment.
motivations.Peeta: Keep the narrative steady and protect Katniss emotionally.
motivations.Haymitch: Maintain discipline and read political signals from each crowd.
motivations.Effie: Keep the schedule perfect and media-ready.

session_desc: District 8 square — Katniss senses organized defiance in the crowd; the visit feels like a rehearsal for something larger.

motivations.Katniss: Understand what’s happening without giving Peacekeepers a reason to target her.
motivations.Peeta: Stay calm and keep attention on their 'love story'.
motivations.District 8 crowd: Test the limits of public defiance and signal readiness to resist.

session_desc: Victory Tour circuit — In Districts 7, 6, and 5, Katniss and Peeta witness the same undercurrent: polite applause masking anger and grief.

motivations.Katniss: Keep responses measured so no one in District 12 pays for it.
motivations.Peeta: Project warmth and stability to avoid giving the Capitol an excuse to escalate.
motivations.Crowds: Communicate dissent without drawing immediate retaliation.

session_desc: Districts 4 and 3 — Katniss sees similar rebellious sentiment as in District 8, confirming that unrest is widespread.

motivations.Katniss: Track how widespread the unrest is and stay alive politically.
motivations.Peeta: Keep Katniss grounded and steer their public message toward empathy.
motivations.Crowds: Signal unity against the Capitol while staying just within the rules.

session_desc: Districts 2 and 1 — The visits are emotionally fraught because these districts produced tributes who died in the 74th Games, and Katniss is blamed in the Capitol narrative.

motivations.Katniss: Avoid provoking hostility while carrying guilt and fear.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss and keep the visit from spiraling.
motivations.Haymitch: Keep them focused on survival, not feelings.

session_desc: Training Center stage — Katniss and Peeta stage a public proposal; Snow appears to congratulate them while silently judging whether they’ve quelled unrest.

motivations.Katniss: Perform commitment convincingly to protect District 12.
motivations.Peeta: Use sincerity and showmanship to make the act believable.
motivations.Snow: Measure whether the victors can be controlled—or must be crushed.
motivations.Caesar Flickerman: Turn the moment into compelling Capitol entertainment.

beat_label: Back to District 12; revolt in the air
session_desc: District 12 — Katniss and Peeta attend the Harvest Festival at Mayor Undersee’s house and glimpse classified intelligence about unrest in other districts.

motivations.Katniss: Understand the danger level without drawing attention.
motivations.Peeta: Stay close and keep Katniss steady.
motivations.Haymitch: Watch for signs of Capitol retaliation.
motivations.Madge: Support Katniss quietly in a hostile environment.
motivations.Mayor Undersee: Maintain a fragile peace in District 12.

session_desc: District 12 train platform — Katniss, Peeta, Haymitch, Effie, and the prep team leave at noon to begin the Victory Tour under intense scrutiny.

motivations.Katniss: Hold herself together and follow the script to keep everyone safe.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss while trying to make their public story believable.
motivations.Haymitch: Coach them to survive Capitol politics.
motivations.Effie: Execute the tour flawlessly for Capitol audiences.

session_desc: District 11 square — Peacekeepers violently suppress the crowd’s defiance, making clear that any public dissent will be punished.

motivations.Peacekeepers: Deter rebellion through fear and immediate punishment.
motivations.Katniss: Stay composed despite the brutality and keep Peeta safe.
motivations.Peeta: Keep Katniss from reacting in a way that puts them all in danger.

session_desc: Train at night — Katniss and Peeta privately process what they saw, realizing the tour is not calming unrest the way Snow demanded.

motivations.Katniss: Figure out how to survive Snow’s expectations when the districts are already boiling.
motivations.Peeta: Reassure Katniss and help craft a safer public strategy.
motivations.Haymitch: Push them toward choices that reduce risk, even if it hurts.

session_desc: President’s mansion party — Katniss meets Plutarch Heavensbee, who subtly hints that the next arena may work like a clock.

motivations.Katniss: Figure out whether she’s being warned or tested.
motivations.Plutarch: Signal inside knowledge to a potential rebel symbol without exposing himself.

session_desc: Across Panem — While the Capitol celebrates, District 8 uses the nighttime programming as cover to launch a full-scale uprising.

motivations.District 8 rebels: Exploit the moment to mobilize openly.
motivations.Peacekeepers: Restore order quickly to prevent contagion across districts.

session_desc: District 8 — Peacekeepers suppress the uprising quickly, impose a lockdown, and broadcast punishment to intimidate other districts.

motivations.Peacekeepers: Use fear to deter copycat revolts.
motivations.District 8 civilians: Survive under collective punishment while sustaining resistance networks.

session_desc: District 12 — A harsher Head Peacekeeper, Romulus Thread, replaces Cray, signaling the Capitol’s crackdown.

motivations.Thread: Impose fear and obedience through strict enforcement.
motivations.District 12 residents: Avoid punishment while adapting to the new regime.

session_desc: District 12 square — Thread installs heavy weapons, whipping posts, and a gallows, reshaping daily life into constant intimidation.

motivations.Thread: Transform the square into a visible threat to crush morale.
motivations.District 12 residents: Keep their heads down and protect their families.

session_desc: District 8 → rail line — After the crackdown, the Capitol destroys the factory tied to the uprising; two refugees, Bonnie and Twill, escape and head toward District 13 rumors.

motivations.Bonnie: Stay alive and reach a place the Capitol can’t reach.
motivations.Twill: Protect her companion and pursue the chance that District 13 still exists.

session_desc: Town square — Gale is arrested and publicly whipped; Katniss intervenes and is struck, while Peeta and Haymitch de-escalate to prevent escalation.

motivations.Gale: Provide for his family despite tightening rules.
motivations.Katniss: Protect Gale and her community even at personal risk.
motivations.Peeta: Prevent Katniss from being killed for defiance.
motivations.Haymitch: Stop the situation from turning into a pretext to target the victors.

session_desc: District 12 — Peacekeepers burn the Hob, cutting off informal trade and tightening the Capitol’s control over food and movement.

motivations.Peacekeepers: Eliminate unsanctioned markets that enable resistance.
motivations.Katniss: Find new ways to feed people and keep independence alive.
motivations.Gale: Protect his family as survival options vanish.

session_desc: Victors’ Village — Gale is treated by Katniss’s mother; Madge brings morphling for pain as a blizzard seals District 12 in isolation.

motivations.Mrs. Everdeen: Keep Gale alive and reduce suffering.
motivations.Madge: Help the Hawthornes and Katniss discreetly.
motivations.Katniss: Hold her circle together under threat.

session_desc: District 12 — With mines closed and supplies failing, hunger spikes; families take tesserae, wages fall, and Parcel Day deliveries arrive spoiled.

motivations.Katniss: Prevent starvation without giving Peacekeepers excuses to punish her.
motivations.Gale: Keep his siblings alive while resentment hardens.
motivations.Hazelle: Hold the household together under worsening scarcity.

beat_label: Wedding pressure and rumors of District 13
session_desc: Victors’ Village — A crate of wedding dresses arrives, reminding Katniss that her private life is being weaponized as propaganda.

motivations.Katniss: Keep up appearances while feeling trapped.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss and prepare for the next political move.
motivations.Haymitch: Keep them alive by managing Capitol expectations.

session_desc: Victors’ Village — Katniss persuades Haymitch to hire Hazelle Hawthorne, creating a lifeline for the Hawthorne family under the new regime.

motivations.Katniss: Use what little power she has to protect friends.
motivations.Haymitch: Stabilize his household and quietly help the Hawthornes.
motivations.Hazelle: Secure income to keep her children alive.

beat_label: Wedding pressure and rumors of District 13
session_title: Bonnie and Twill at the lake
session_desc: Outside District 12 — Katniss meets refugees Bonnie and Twill, who speak of rumors that District 13 still exists; Katniss is trapped by an electrified fence and injures herself escaping.

motivations.Katniss: Verify whether hope beyond the Capitol is real while avoiding capture.
motivations.Bonnie: Reach District 13 as a last refuge.
motivations.Twill: Protect Bonnie and keep moving before Peacekeepers find them.

beat_label: Wedding pressure and rumors of District 13
session_desc: District 12 — Peacekeepers inform Katniss that the fence will now be electrified around the clock, closing off the woods as an escape route.

motivations.Peacekeepers: Remove pathways that enable poaching and movement.
motivations.Katniss: Find any remaining space for freedom and survival.

beat_label: Signals from the past: District 13 footage
session_desc: Everdeen home — While Katniss recovers, Peeta visits daily, bringing food and helping with the plant book, trying to create stability under siege.

motivations.Katniss: Heal while feeling increasingly powerless.
motivations.Peeta: Keep Katniss grounded and emotionally supported.

beat_label: Signals from the past: District 13 footage
session_desc: Television — Katniss notices repeated 'live' footage of District 13 ruins, reinforcing the idea that the Capitol may be hiding the truth.

motivations.Katniss: Make sense of the propaganda and decide what’s real.

beat_label: Katniss is back on her feet
session_desc: Victors’ Village — Katniss plans to re-enter daily life after injury, hoping movement will restore some control.

motivations.Katniss: Reclaim normal routines and autonomy.

beat_label: Cinna’s early arrival and the photoshoot
session_desc: Victors’ Village — Cinna and the prep team arrive early for a wedding-themed photoshoot, turning Katniss into a symbol the Capitol can package.

motivations.Katniss: Endure the spectacle without breaking.
motivations.Cinna: Protect Katniss through careful presentation while embedding subversive meaning where possible.

beat_label: Cinna’s early arrival and the photoshoot
session_desc: District 12 news and imports — Shortages from Districts 4, 3, and 8 are explained away, but suggest sustained unrest across Panem.

motivations.Katniss: Read the political temperature and anticipate danger.
motivations.Peeta: Keep Katniss focused and safe while the situation worsens.

session_title: Special broadcast with Caesar and Cinna
session_desc: Capitol broadcast — Caesar hosts a special featuring Katniss’s gowns, building toward a public narrative that suddenly turns ominous.

motivations.Caesar Flickerman: Keep the Capitol audience engaged with glamour.
motivations.Cinna: Use fashion and staging to shape perception of Katniss.
motivations.Katniss: Survive being turned into a spectacle.

session_desc: Capitol — Snow announces that tributes for the 75th Hunger Games will be reaped from existing victors, making Katniss a target again.

motivations.Snow: Crush the symbol of defiance by forcing victors back into the arena.
motivations.Katniss: Protect Peeta and her loved ones despite the trap closing.
motivations.Haymitch: Plan around an impossible rule to keep his tributes alive.
motivations.Peeta: Prepare to sacrifice himself if needed to save Katniss.

session_title: Katniss and Haymitch commit to protect Peeta
session_desc: Victors’ Village — After the announcement, Katniss and Haymitch decide they will do whatever it takes to keep Peeta alive if the Games happen.

motivations.Katniss: Make Peeta’s survival the priority, even over her own.
motivations.Haymitch: Turn strategy into protection for the only people he can still save.

session_title: Peeta cuts off Haymitch’s liquor access
session_desc: District 12 — Peeta pressures Ripper and dumps Haymitch’s liquor, forcing discipline as they prepare for the Quell.

motivations.Peeta: Get the team functional and focused for survival.
motivations.Haymitch: Resist change but recognize the stakes.
motivations.Katniss: Accept hard constraints to improve their odds.
motivations.Ripper: Avoid punishment and keep her own position stable.

session_desc: Victors’ Village — Katniss, Peeta, and Haymitch begin daily training: endurance, combat skills, and studying previous victors’ Games.

motivations.Katniss: Build capability without losing her humanity.
motivations.Peeta: Prepare to protect Katniss and manage alliances.
motivations.Haymitch: Translate experience into a plan that might work.

session_desc: District 12 — Through spring into early summer, the trio trains daily and watches Games recaps, anticipating a Quell designed to kill favorites.

motivations.Katniss: Avoid being helpless when the Capitol strikes again.
motivations.Peeta: Become useful in any alliance and keep Katniss alive.
motivations.Haymitch: Identify strengths, weaknesses, and likely arena patterns.

session_desc: District 12 — Katniss and Haymitch are selected under the Quell rule; Peeta volunteers in Haymitch’s place, forcing the trio into a new life-or-death cycle.

motivations.Katniss: Protect Peeta while facing the Capitol again.
motivations.Peeta: Take Haymitch’s place to keep Katniss from being alone.
motivations.Haymitch: Manage the shock and pivot immediately to survival strategy.
motivations.Effie: Hold the ceremony together despite its cruelty.

session_desc: Train to the Capitol — The tributes are denied time with family and rushed directly onto the train, emphasizing the Capitol’s control.

motivations.Peacekeepers: Prevent any public scenes or organizing in District 12.
motivations.Katniss: Stay calm and focus on what comes next.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss through the abrupt separation.
motivations.Haymitch: Begin planning alliances immediately.

session_desc: Capitol — Katniss and Peeta meet Finnick Odair and Johanna Mason, realizing alliances among victors may be possible.

motivations.Katniss: Assess who can be trusted among experienced victors.
motivations.Peeta: Build rapport to protect Katniss through alliance.
motivations.Finnick: Gauge whether joining Katniss helps his own survival and resistance goals.
motivations.Johanna: Project toughness while deciding how to play the political game.
motivations.Haymitch: Map the social terrain fast.

session_desc: Capitol streets — The victors are displayed in a parade, turning terror into entertainment while the Capitol audience judges them.

motivations.Katniss: Stay composed under scrutiny.
motivations.Peeta: Keep up the public narrative while watching for signals.
motivations.Capitol citizens: Consume the spectacle and pick favorites.

session_desc: Training Center — Katniss’s archery impresses other victors, and many approach her for alliance talks.

motivations.Katniss: Show competence without becoming a target.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss and negotiate alliances.
motivations.Others: Choose partners who increase their survival odds and political leverage.

session_desc: Training Center — In his private session, Peeta creates a tribute to Rue, using artistry to force the Capitol to confront what it kills.

motivations.Peeta: Humanize the victims and provoke empathy in the audience.

session_title: Katniss defies with a target dummy
session_desc: Training Center — Katniss stages a symbolic act of defiance in her private session, earning attention and risk at once.

motivations.Katniss: Channel anger into a statement while proving she’s not powerless.

session_desc: Training Center rooftop — Katniss and Peeta choose a calm moment together instead of rehearsing for interviews, reaffirming what they’re fighting for.

motivations.Katniss: Hold onto something real amid manipulation.
motivations.Peeta: Give Katniss comfort and a sense of agency.

session_desc: Capitol stage — Multiple victors use interviews to plead, protest, or appeal to the crowd, building sympathy even if the Games continue.

motivations.Victors: Pressure the Capitol by turning popularity into moral outrage.
motivations.Caesar Flickerman: Contain the emotion while keeping the show moving.

session_desc: Capitol stage — Katniss’s wedding dress transforms into a mockingjay symbol, electrifying the audience and provoking the Capitol leadership.

motivations.Katniss: Survive the moment while realizing she’s become a symbol.
motivations.Cinna: Use design to empower Katniss and signal resistance.
motivations.Snow: Clamp down on symbolism that threatens authority.

session_desc: Capitol stage — Peeta makes a shocking claim to sway the audience against the Games, triggering visible unrest as the interviews are cut short.

motivations.Peeta: Force the Capitol to see Katniss as a person, not a pawn.
motivations.Katniss: Keep composure while the narrative spins out of control.
motivations.Capitol crowd: React emotionally to the cruelty made explicit.

session_desc: Arena launch — The Quell begins under Plutarch’s direction; the victors are sent into an arena designed as a deadly clockwork trap.

motivations.Katniss: Find Peeta and stay alive long enough to act.
motivations.Peeta: Protect Katniss through alliances and positioning.
motivations.Plutarch: Run the Games while quietly steering toward a larger plan.

session_desc: Jungle perimeter — Katniss and Peeta commit to an alliance with Finnick and Mags; early chaos forces fast trust decisions.

motivations.Katniss: Trust enough to survive without losing control.
motivations.Peeta: Build a protective coalition.
motivations.Finnick: Keep Mags safe and align with people tied to resistance.

beat_label: The arena clock reveals its pattern
session_desc: Arena — The victors realize the arena’s dangers follow a repeating schedule, turning survival into pattern recognition and timing.

motivations.Katniss: Learn the pattern fast to avoid predictable hazards.
motivations.Wiress: Decode the arena structure despite stress.
motivations.Beetee: Convert understanding into a plan to change the game.

beat_label: The arena clock reveals its pattern
session_desc: Arena jungle — Alliances strain as hazards and fatigue accumulate, forcing choices about who to help and how to move.

motivations.Johanna: Keep herself alive while hiding deeper intentions.
motivations.Katniss: Hold the alliance together long enough to protect Peeta.
motivations.Beetee: Preserve trust to execute a larger plan.

session_desc: Arena — Beetee pushes a plan involving a coil of wire and a targeted strike, aiming to disrupt the arena’s systems rather than just survive it.

motivations.Beetee: Exploit technology to undermine the Capitol’s control.
motivations.Katniss: Follow the plan while protecting Peeta.
motivations.Johanna: Play her role in a coordinated breakout.
motivations.Finnick: Support the plan that aligns with resistance.

session_desc: Arena boundary — The arena’s force field is breached; chaos follows as a rescue operation pulls select victors out, ending the Games abruptly.

motivations.Rebel rescuers: Extract the symbol and key allies to fuel rebellion.
motivations.Plutarch: Transition from Gamemaker to rebel coordinator without exposure.
motivations.Katniss: Survive the sudden shift and find Peeta.

session_desc: Panem — News spreads that District 7 rises against the Capitol and District 5 is taken over, marking the rebellion’s escalation beyond isolated uprisings.

motivations.Rebels: Turn scattered defiance into coordinated revolt.
motivations.Capitol forces: Contain the rebellion before it becomes irreversible.

session_desc: District 13 — Katniss learns she has been rescued by rebels; the 'Games' were broken, and a larger war has begun.

motivations.Katniss: Understand what happened and locate Peeta.
motivations.District 13 leaders: Use Katniss as a rallying symbol while keeping operations secure.
motivations.Plutarch: Explain enough to earn trust without revealing every compromise.

session_title: Peeta and Johanna captured; District 12 destroyed
session_desc: District 13 briefing — Katniss is told Peeta and Johanna were taken by the Capitol, and District 12 has been destroyed in retaliation.

motivations.Katniss: Process grief and rage while deciding what to do next.
motivations.Peeta: Endure captivity while trying to protect Katniss in any way he can.
motivations.Johanna: Survive captivity after committing to rebellion.
motivations.Gale: Survive the destruction and find any remaining people.

session_desc: 0075-07-20 to 0075-07-31 — Panem learns District 13 survived underground and is leading the rebel war effort.

motivations.Katniss: Figure out what the rebellion expects of her while still reeling from loss and trauma.
motivations.Coin: Unify the districts under District 13’s leadership and legitimize the rebellion publicly.
motivations.Plutarch: Use media and strategy to turn scattered unrest into coordinated rebellion.

session_desc: District 12 ruins — Katniss visits the ashes; a Capitol interview of Peeta airs; Katniss agrees to become the Mockingjay.

motivations.Katniss: Confront what was lost and decide whether to become the rebellion’s symbol.
motivations.Peeta: Survive captivity and attempt to communicate with Katniss under Capitol control.
motivations.Gale: Support the survivors and push the rebellion forward.
motivations.Coin: Secure Katniss’s commitment as propaganda leader.

session_desc: District 13 — Katniss negotiates terms (including conditions about Peeta) and Coin announces the deal to District 13.

motivations.Katniss: Set terms that protect people she cares about and keep some personal agency.
motivations.Coin: Lock in the Mockingjay as a controlled asset for the rebellion.
motivations.Plutarch: Shape the deal into a message that motivates mass resistance.
motivations.Haymitch: Back Katniss while trying to keep her alive and functional.

session_desc: District 8 — Katniss films a propo; the field hospital is bombed; she and Gale help take down hovercraft and capture footage.

motivations.Katniss: Turn anger and grief into a message that convinces districts to keep fighting.
motivations.Gale: Protect Katniss and strike back at Capitol forces when possible.
motivations.Coin: Broadcast compelling images to accelerate uprisings.
motivations.Plutarch: Craft a narrative that makes rebellion feel inevitable.

session_desc: Broadcast — Peeta appears again on Capitol television as propaganda continues to pressure Katniss and the rebels.

motivations.Peeta: Endure propaganda use while trying not to endanger others.
motivations.Katniss: Stay steady and avoid being manipulated by the Capitol’s message.
motivations.Coin: Use the broadcast to justify urgency and unify rebel sentiment.

session_desc: Districts 12/13 — Rebel morale rises; Districts 3 and 11 fall to rebels; Katniss and crew film in District 12 and she sings “The Hanging Tree.”

motivations.Katniss: Offer a personal, haunting symbol that people can rally around.
motivations.Gale: Record the truth of District 12’s destruction and strengthen rebel resolve.
motivations.Plutarch: Deploy a powerful cultural message to spread resistance fast.
motivations.Beetee: Exploit broadcast windows and communications for strategic advantage.

session_desc: Broadcast/District 13 — During a live interview, Peeta warns of an imminent air strike; District 13 evacuates into bunkers.

motivations.Peeta: Get a warning out despite coercion, hoping to save lives.
motivations.Katniss: React fast and keep District 13 from collapsing into panic.
motivations.Coin: Protect the district and preserve command continuity.
motivations.Beetee: Secure systems and keep communications running under attack.

session_desc: 0075-08-27 to 0075-08-29 — District 13 is targeted by bunker missiles over several days; the district survives due to evacuation.

motivations.Katniss: Hold together mentally while being used as a symbol under real threat.
motivations.Coin: Prove District 13’s resilience and keep the rebellion’s leadership alive.
motivations.Beetee: Maintain defenses and technical readiness during sustained strikes.

session_desc: District 13 — After quiet returns, Katniss and Finnick attempt propos but break down; both are sedated while Boggs plans a rescue of captured victors.

motivations.Katniss: Try to keep functioning as the Mockingjay despite trauma.
motivations.Finnick: Push through grief and fear while helping the rebellion’s message.
motivations.Boggs: Prepare a high-risk extraction to recover key hostages.
motivations.Coin: Keep the Mockingjay presentable and the rebellion on schedule.

session_desc: District 13/Capitol — Katniss and Finnick film distraction propos; District 13 commandos infiltrate the Capitol and secure Peeta, Annie, and Johanna.

motivations.Katniss: Do her part to cover the rescue while staying emotionally grounded.
motivations.Finnick: Support the operation and keep the public message strong.
motivations.Boggs: Execute the extraction with minimal losses.
motivations.Peeta: Survive long enough to be rescued, even while manipulated.
motivations.Johanna: Endure captivity and prepare to recover enough to fight back.
motivations.Annie: Survive imprisonment and hold onto hope.

session_desc: District 13 — The rescued victors arrive; Peeta is revealed to have been hijacked using tracker jacker venom, making him dangerous to Katniss.

motivations.Katniss: Protect herself and others while trying not to lose Peeta entirely.
motivations.Peeta: Fight distorted memories and regain control of his reality.
motivations.Coin: Contain risk and keep the Mockingjay from being harmed on camera.
motivations.Dr. Aurelius: Stabilize Peeta and assess trauma across the victors.

session_desc: September 75 ADD — Rebels begin their final campaign to take District 2, the Capitol’s military stronghold.

motivations.Katniss: Join the push to end the war while still acting as a symbol.
motivations.Gale: Help win the war decisively and protect Katniss where he can.
motivations.Paylor: Lead ground strategy and coordinate liberated districts.
motivations.Lyme: Command forces against the Capitol’s most entrenched defenses.

session_desc: Late September 75 ADD — Rebels destroy ‘the Nut’ command center; District 2 falls; Katniss is shot during a live assassination attempt but survives.

motivations.Katniss: Survive and keep the Mockingjay’s image intact for the movement.
motivations.Gale: Finish the operation even under chaos and protect allies.
motivations.Paylor: Collapse Capitol command capability to end the war faster.
motivations.Coin: Capitalize on victory and maintain political control of the rebellion.

session_desc: Autumn 75 ADD — Annie and Finnick’s wedding is broadcast as a propo to inspire the districts and show normal life returning.

motivations.Finnick: Claim a moment of hope and humanity amid war.
motivations.Annie: Hold onto love and stability after trauma.
motivations.Katniss: Draw strength from allies’ resilience and keep moving forward.
motivations.Plutarch: Use a hopeful broadcast to strengthen commitment to the cause.

session_desc: Autumn 75 ADD — Katniss and Johanna train for the Capitol assault; Johanna is deemed unfit after a traumatic breakdown.

motivations.Katniss: Earn a role in the final push toward the Capitol.
motivations.Johanna: Try to regain control of her fear and prove she can fight.
motivations.Haymitch: Keep the remaining victors alive and functional.
motivations.Dr. Aurelius: Evaluate who is fit to deploy and prevent collapse.

session_desc: Late autumn 75 ADD — Rebels launch a full assault on the Capitol; pods and traps slow the advance as Peacekeepers fall back into the city.

motivations.Katniss: Get to Snow and end the war on her terms.
motivations.Boggs: Guide the propaganda unit through an active combat zone.
motivations.Paylor: Win the city without losing the political legitimacy of the rebels.
motivations.Plutarch: Treat the battlefield like an arena and manage public perception.

session_desc: Late autumn 75 ADD — Squad 451 is transported to District 12, travels by train and tunnel, and reaches the rebel encampment near the Capitol.

motivations.Katniss: Stay with the unit long enough to reach Snow.
motivations.Boggs: Keep the squad alive and on mission despite Katniss’s unpredictability.
motivations.Finnick: Protect the team and keep Katniss steady.
motivations.Jackson: Lead tactically and adapt to pods and urban warfare.

session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 4 after arrival: Squad 451 suffers casualties when a pod kills Leeg 2.

motivations.Katniss: Push forward even as losses mount.
motivations.Boggs: Hold the unit together and keep morale from breaking.
motivations.Leeg 2: Do her job in the assault despite deadly uncertainty.
motivations.Jackson: Keep the squad moving and prevent panic.

session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 5: Peeta arrives to replace Leeg 2 in the unit.

motivations.Katniss: Manage fear and protect the mission while near hijacked Peeta.
motivations.Peeta: Prove he can control himself and contribute.
motivations.Boggs: Use Peeta but minimize risk to Katniss and team.
motivations.Jackson: Integrate a volatile member into a dangerous mission.

session_title: Coping strategy: Real or Not Real
session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 6: Jackson invents ‘Real or Not Real’ to help Peeta distinguish hijacked memories from reality.

motivations.Peeta: Rebuild trust in his own mind and reduce danger to others.
motivations.Katniss: Help Peeta recover while staying focused on survival.
motivations.Jackson: Keep the unit functioning by stabilizing Peeta.

session_title: Boggs fatally wounded; Katniss takes the Holo
session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 7: Boggs is mortally wounded by a pod and transfers the Holo to Katniss; she leads an unauthorized push to assassinate Snow.

motivations.Katniss: Seize control of her own mission and reach Snow.
motivations.Boggs: Ensure the mission continues even if he can’t.
motivations.Gale: Pursue the war’s end while staying aligned with Katniss.
motivations.Finnick: Keep Katniss alive through escalating danger.

session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 8: Squad 451 enters the sewers; most die to lizard mutts, including Finnick; survivors shelter at Tigris’s shop.

motivations.Katniss: Survive long enough to reach Snow, despite losing friends.
motivations.Peeta: Stay controlled and protect the others in close quarters.
motivations.Finnick: Keep the squad alive, even at personal cost.
motivations.Tigris: Offer refuge and resist Snow’s regime in the only way she can.

session_desc: Battle timeline — Days 9–10: The survivors hide with Tigris, monitor broadcasts, and plan a route toward Snow’s mansion.

motivations.Katniss: Recover enough to keep moving toward the endgame.
motivations.Peeta: Hold steady and avoid harming Katniss.
motivations.Tigris: Help rebels survive and undermine the Capitol quietly.
motivations.Gale: Advance with rebel forces while trying to find Katniss.

session_desc: Battle timeline — Day 11: Katniss reaches City Circle; a bombing kills Prim; Gale is captured; Katniss is incapacitated.

motivations.Katniss: Reach Snow and end the war, unaware of the trap ahead.
motivations.Prim: Help as a medic, believing she is saving lives.
motivations.Gale: Fight for victory, but is caught in the chaos.
motivations.Snow: Maintain control by turning the city into a final psychological arena.

session_desc: After the bombing — Support for Snow collapses; rebels take the Capitol; the Second Rebellion ends and remaining victors stop being targeted.

motivations.Snow: Survive the collapse long enough to frame his legacy and enemies.
motivations.Coin: Assume control of Panem’s transition and consolidate authority.
motivations.Paylor: Stabilize the new government with legitimacy and order.
motivations.Katniss: Endure the aftermath and decide what justice should look like.

session_title: Snow tried; truth about the bombing
session_desc: Winter 75 ADD — Snow is tried and sentenced; he claims the City Circle bombing was Coin’s false-flag operation using District 13 bombers.

motivations.Snow: Sow doubt and revenge by implicating Coin.
motivations.Katniss: Understand who truly killed Prim and choose her response.
motivations.Coin: Proceed with transition while controlling the narrative.
motivations.Paylor: Keep the fragile peace and manage legitimacy.

session_desc: Winter 75 ADD — Before Snow’s execution, victors vote on a symbolic 76th Hunger Games (never held). At the execution, Katniss assassinates Coin; Snow dies in the chaos.

motivations.Katniss: Prevent another tyrant from replacing Snow and end the cycle.
motivations.Coin: Secure power through spectacle and punitive policy.
motivations.Snow: Exploit the moment to ensure his enemies destroy each other.
motivations.Haymitch: Back Katniss’s judgment while protecting what remains of their group.
motivations.Peeta: Support Katniss and choose a future beyond violence.
motivations.Johanna: Vent rage but also seek an end to being used.

session_desc: 76 ADD (unknown months) — Katniss, Peeta, and Haymitch assemble a memory book; District 12 slowly rebuilds with new agriculture and industry, and trauma recovery continues.

motivations.Katniss: Hold onto the truth of what happened without being consumed by it.
motivations.Peeta: Make healing tangible through routine and shared memory.
motivations.Haymitch: Honor the dead while surviving the living aftermath.
motivations.Beetee: Redirect technology toward reconstruction and public good.

session_desc: Dec–Feb 76 ADD — An emergency election installs Paylor as president. Katniss is held in the Training Center during legal proceedings and is eventually released under restrictions.

motivations.Paylor: Build a democratic government and prevent another dictatorship.
motivations.Katniss: Survive judgment and find a way to live after war.
motivations.Plutarch: Protect allies and shape the new political order.
motivations.Dr. Aurelius: Argue for treatment and healing over punishment.

session_desc: Early spring 76 ADD — Peeta returns to District 12; crews clear rubble and bury bodies; Katniss finds Buttercup and begins to heal.

motivations.Katniss: Mourn, heal, and rebuild a life in the ruins of home.
motivations.Peeta: Help rebuild and re-establish trust and daily stability.
motivations.Haymitch: Stay present as a fragile anchor for both of them.

session_desc: 77–90 ADD — Panem remains at relative peace as a democracy; past arenas are demolished and memorials are built in their place.

motivations.Paylor: Keep institutions stable so peace lasts beyond the revolution.
motivations.Katniss: Live quietly and carry memory without reliving the arena.
motivations.Peeta: Build a home and future that rejects the old spectacle.

session_desc: 96 ADD — In the Mockingjay epilogue, Katniss watches her children play in the Meadow, reflecting on memory and survival.

motivations.Katniss: Keep living despite fear, using memory as a coping practice.
motivations.Peeta: Maintain a gentle, grounded life built from small daily choices.
